signals.evidence: Mobile SSO entry point conflates a transient PM-side introspection outage with a genuinely invalid token, returning 401. `create_mobile_sso_token` (backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:450-499) calls `introspect_pm_token(...)` and maps ANY Err to `(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, 'invalid_token')` (sso.rs:456-462). But `introspect_pm_token_inner` (sso.rs:796-857) was DELIBERATELY hardened to return an Err WITHOUT caching on any non-2xx introspection response — a PM 5xx outage, 502/504 gateway error, or transport error — precisely because such a response is 'not a genuine active=false verdict' (per the Epic 104.2 negative-cache-poisoning guard comment). The handler discards that carefully-preserved distinction: during a transient PM introspection outage a mobile client presenting a perfectly valid token receives 401 invalid_token, which signals 'your credentials are bad' and can cause the client to discard/clear otherwise-valid credentials and force a spurious re-login. The transport-layer effort to distinguish outage-from-inactive is negated at the handler boundary. Recommend surfacing PM outage/5xx/transport errors as 502 Bad Gateway or 503 Service Unavailable (retryable) rather than 401, so clients back off and retry instead of treating the token as invalid. The same collapse-to-401 also applies to the `get_user_info` failure branch (sso.rs:472-479) and `refresh_session` (sso.rs:613-626).

A realtor-facing DB write Result is silently discarded with no logging, so read-state desync is unobservable. In the realtor inquiry-detail path (backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/inquiries.rs:700-704) the code does `let _ = state.reality_portal_repo.mark_inquiry_read_for_realtor(id, principal.user_id).await;` — the Result of a DB UPDATE that marks the inquiry read is dropped entirely (no `?`, no `map_err`, no `tracing::warn`). Ownership is already verified above so this is not an authz bug, but unlike the truly fire-and-forget analytics call at listings.rs:370 (`track_view`), inquiry read-state is user-visible: if the UPDATE fails (transient DB error, deadlock, connection drop), the inquiry keeps showing as unread on every subsequent load with zero operator visibility into why. Contrast with the deliberate, commented discard in saved_search_alerts.rs:223. Recommend at minimum logging the failure (`if let Err(e) = ... { tracing::warn!(inquiry_id = %id, error = %e, "failed to mark inquiry read"); }`) so the desync is diagnosable.
